meta.title: FHIR Clinical CDR
meta.summary: A portable FHIR resource-store model that preserves canonical resources, makes MongoDB operational projections explicit, and translates supported FHIR Search parameters to inspectable MQL.

fhir_resource.definition: A canonical FHIR JSON resource whose concrete shape T is selected by the `resourceType` discriminator and activated release. R4 currently exposes a minimal Patient/Observation contract; R5/R6 are package-backed.

logical_identity.definition: FHIR ids are unique within a resource type. The store therefore identifies a resource by `(resourceType, id)` and enforces `id` uniqueness inside each per-type collection.

choice_element.definition: A polymorphic FHIR element represented by one type-specific JSON property, such as `Observation.valueQuantity` or `Observation.valueCodeableConcept`. The model displays the abstract form as `value[x]`.

reference.definition: A FHIR reference whose permitted target types are defined by the resource specification or profile. It is a domain relationship, not an automatic MongoDB join.

extension.definition: FHIR extension content remains canonical JSON. Primitive-extension properties such as `_birthDate` are preserved; only the accelerator's documented operational fields are removed from FHIR-facing responses.

profile.definition: A StructureDefinition that constrains a base FHIR resource. This CDR currently preserves profile declarations but does not claim profile, invariant, reference, or terminology validation.

search_parameter.definition: A named FHIR query parameter with a type and extraction expression. Support is resolved per resource type from the active fhir-mql configuration rather than inferred from the JSON shape alone.

operational_projection.definition: Mandatory MongoDB-only `_search` and `_compartments` projections plus versioned persistence metadata grouped under `_kehrnel`. These fields are never returned as FHIR content.

collection_family.definition: An abstract family of MongoDB collections. A concrete collection is created or used when a supported resource type is persisted, with an optional configured prefix followed by the exact `resourceType`.

cohort_blueprint.definition: A versioned, portable intent document that defines patient demographics, resource-count distributions, longitudinal scope, and named clinical rules. Kehrnel compiles it into a deterministic plan before any data is generated; curated-demo does not claim epidemiological or clinical validity.

types.title: FHIR Resource<T>
types.description: The common FHIR resource metamodel. T is a concrete resource shape from the activated release support tier.

resourceType.description: Selects the concrete resource shape and MongoDB collection.

id.description: Logical id, unique only within the concrete resource type.

meta.description: FHIR metadata including version, lastUpdated, profile, security, and tags when present.

extension[].description: Standard FHIR extension mechanism retained in canonical form.

primitiveExtension.description: FHIR primitive extensions such as `_birthDate`; these are not MongoDB operational fields.

choice[x].description: Exactly the type-specific JSON property allowed by the concrete resource/profile, for example `valueQuantity`.

reference.description: A reference to one of the target types allowed by the concrete resource/profile.

payload<T>.description: All remaining fields defined for concrete resource type T.

concepts.title: Discriminated resource polymorphism
concepts.meaning: One common Resource metamodel expands to many concrete JSON shapes. `resourceType` is both the FHIR discriminator and the collection-routing key.

concepts.title: Choice elements
concepts.meaning: FHIR `[x]` elements become mutually exclusive, type-specific JSON properties. MongoDB preserves the selected property without flattening it into a generic value column.

concepts.title: Polymorphic references
concepts.meaning: Fields such as `Observation.subject` may target several resource types. Search projections may accelerate reference filters, but they do not change reference semantics or imply joins.

concepts.title: Canonical / operational boundary
concepts.meaning: Canonical FHIR fields stay readable at the document root. MongoDB-only projections are explicitly denylisted and removed from FHIR serialization.

concepts.title: FHIR Search compilation
concepts.meaning: The active resource configuration maps supported FHIR Search parameters to typed MongoDB filters and index definitions. Unknown parameters fail closed in strict mode.

destinations.description: One abstract collection family materializes concrete collections on demand. The entries below are representative clinical examples, not a fixed claim about every resource type supported by the active runtime.

encodingProfiles.title: Canonical FHIR JSON at document root
encodingProfiles.description: FHIR property names, nesting, arrays, choice elements, extensions, and primitive extensions remain recognizable. Activation selects the R4, R5, or R6 support tier.

operationalProjection.description: Implementation fields stored atomically with the canonical resource and removed from FHIR-facing responses.

fields._search: Typed search-parameter projections generated from the active fhir-mql resource configuration.
fields._compartments: Resolved compartment memberships such as `_compartments.Patient` when configured.
fields._kehrnel: Kehrnel-owned metadata: stored-document schema version, global and per-resource projection versions, FHIR release, and persistence/projection timestamps.
fields._custom: Customer-owned non-FHIR data preserved across canonical resource updates.
fields._enrichments: Partner or accelerator enrichment data preserved across canonical resource updates.

indexContract.description: Identity and search indexes have different sources of truth. The storage adapter enforces logical-id uniqueness; fhir-mql supplies search index definitions for the resource types supported by the active configuration.

search.note: Use the runtime dry-run result to review exact collection names, fields, and options before applying indexes. Index use remains query- and selectivity-dependent.

stores.title: Patient
stores.purpose: Representative identity and demographics resource collection.

stores.title: Encounter
stores.purpose: Representative encounter resource collection with references and temporal search parameters.

stores.title: Observation
stores.purpose: Representative high-volume clinical resource demonstrating choice elements, references, codes, quantities, and dates.

stores.title: Condition
stores.purpose: Representative clinical problem resource demonstrating references, coded status, and onset/abatement choice elements.

stores.title: Procedure
stores.purpose: Representative clinical event resource. The concrete temporal choice is release-specific; R5 names it `occurrence[x]`.

stores.title: MedicationRequest
stores.purpose: Representative medication order resource; the concrete medication shape varies by FHIR release.

stores.title: DiagnosticReport
stores.purpose: Representative report resource with result references and effective choice elements.

storePattern.title: Collection<ResourceType>
storePattern.description: A concrete collection follows this pattern when a supported resource type is persisted. The runtime capability response is authoritative for storable, searchable, and generatable resource sets.
storePattern.searchIndexes: resolved from the active fhir-mql configuration

visual.notes: Accept one resource, a Bundle, an array, or NDJSON and normalize it to bounded resource batches.
Enforces safe routing and identity invariants. R5/R6 can use bundled base-schema validation; the provisional R4 tier is structural only. Profile conformance is not claimed.
fhir-mql extracts configured typed search values and compartment memberships into `_search` and `_compartments`.
Resolve `config.collection_prefix + resourceType`; the discriminator is never inferred from another field.
Create or replace by logical id through the storage adapter. The search projection is written atomically with the canonical fields.

invariants: Every persisted resource has a valid non-empty `resourceType` and FHIR logical `id`.
Logical identity is `(resourceType, id)`; `id` is unique inside each per-type collection.
MongoDB-unsafe property names are rejected at the import boundary.
Client-supplied operational fields are removed before validation and projection.
FHIR serialization removes only the explicit operational denylist and preserves primitive-extension fields.
The validation level and resource type must be supported by the activated release tier.

queryModel.summary: FHIR REST interactions and FHIR Search remain the user-facing contract. The compiler makes their MongoDB execution plan visible without claiming unsupported server features.

modes.title: Read by type and logical id
modes.notes: Returns canonical FHIR JSON after removing documented operational fields.

modes.title: Resource-type search
modes.filter: Compiled from the URL/query tuple by the active resource configuration
modes.index: resource-specific runtime index when the query shape matches
modes.notes: Strict handling fails closed on unknown or unsupported parameters. Index use is verified with the generated MQL and MongoDB explain, not guaranteed by the model alone.

modes.title: Compartment search
modes.notes: Available when the active resolver supports the requested compartment/resource combination. It does not assume every patient-related resource uses one generic `_search.patient` field.

modes.title: Compile and inspect
modes.notes: Returns the target collection, MongoDB filter, result controls, and ignored parameters without executing the query. This is the primary learning and migration-debugging workflow in Healthcare Data Lab.

unsupportedBoundaries: Transactions and batches with transactional semantics
Full profile, invariant, reference, and terminology conformance
queryModel.runtimeEvidence: Use `fhir_capabilities` for the active storable, searchable, and generatable resource sets, search-parameter names/types, result controls, validation levels, and profile-conformance flag.

entries.label: choice[x]

entries.label: Reference<T>
entries.meaning: FHIR relationship to one of the allowed target types; not an implicit join

entries.label: _<primitiveName>
entries.meaning: canonical FHIR primitive extension, preserved during serialization

entries.meaning: typed operational search projections generated by fhir-mql

entries.meaning: stored shape and projection versions plus operational timestamps

entries.label: _custom / _enrichments
entries.meaning: reserved partner and customer namespaces preserved atomically across canonical FHIR updates and never returned by the FHIR API

indexOverlay.note: The identity index is fixed by the storage contract. Search indexes are shown from the active fhir-mql configuration and should be verified against real query plans.
